bib.title: LLAMA-OMNI: SEAMLESS SPEECH INTERACTION WITH LARGE LANGUAGE MODELS

question: How can an open-source LLM be given low-latency, high-quality speech-to-speech interaction without a separate ASR/TTS cascade and with little training data and compute?
hypothesis: An LLM with a speech encoder and a CTC-based non-autoregressive streaming speech decoder, trained on speech-style instruction data, can produce text and speech simultaneously with latency below cascaded and prior speech-LMs.
contributions: LLaMA-Omni architecture: speech encoder, speech adaptor, LLM, streaming speech decoder generating text and speech simultaneously
InstructS2S-200K dataset of 200K speech instructions with speech-style responses
Training in under 3 days on 4 GPUs; response latency as low as 236ms

method.summary: Frozen Whisper-large-v3 encoder feeds a trainable adaptor into Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct. A 2-layer NAR Transformer speech decoder takes LLM hidden states (upsampled 25x), predicts HuBERT units with CTC, and a unit HiFi-GAN vocoder synthesizes chunks of Omega units while the LLM still generates text. Two-stage training: adaptor+LLM on text responses, then speech decoder only.

datasets.name: InstructS2S-200K
datasets.size: 200K speech instruction/response triplets; 418h instruction audio, 1058h response audio
datasets.source: Built by authors: ~50K Alpaca instructions + first 150K UltraChat entries (first turn only); rewritten and answered by Llama-3-70B-Instruct; instructions TTS by CosyVoice-300M-SFT (random male/female voice), responses by VITS trained on LJSpeech
datasets.preprocessing: Instruction rewriting (fillers, numbers as words, brief); concise TTS-friendly responses; response units from HuBERT + K-means (1000 clusters), consecutive duplicates merged

datasets.name: InstructS2S-Eval
datasets.source: AlpacaEval subsets helpful_base and vicuna, math and code questions removed; speech via CosyVoice-300M-SFT

models.name: LLaMA-Omni
models.params: inferred: ~8B LLM + Whisper-large-v3 encoder + 425M speech decoder; total not stated
models.architecture: Whisper encoder + 2-layer MLP adaptor (5x downsample) + Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct + NAR CTC streaming Transformer speech decoder + unit HiFi-GAN vocoder

models.name: SALMONN + Orca
models.architecture: speech-to-text LLM + Orca streaming TTS cascade

models.name: Qwen2-Audio + Orca
models.architecture: audio LLM + Orca streaming TTS cascade

models.name: Whisper-large-v3
models.architecture: ASR used to transcribe speech responses for scoring and WER

training.objective: Stage 1: cross-entropy on text response (L_LLM); Stage 2: CTC loss on discrete units (L_CTC)
training.compute: about 65 hours on 4 L40 (less than 3 days)

other.stage2_trainable: speech decoder only (encoder, adaptor, LLM frozen)
other.stage2_schedule: same batch size, steps and scheduler as stage 1

inference.samples: single greedy run per instruction; no seeds
inference.prompting: Llama-3 chat template with system prompt and <speech> placeholder (App. A)

metrics.name: ChatGPT Score
metrics.definition: GPT-4o scores 1-5 on helpfulness, relevance, fluency, suitability for speech; for S2SIF the speech is first transcribed with Whisper-large-v3

metrics.name: ASR-WER
metrics.definition: WER between Whisper-large-v3 transcript of speech response and the model's text response

metrics.name: UTMOS
metrics.definition: MOS prediction model score for naturalness

metrics.name: Latency
metrics.definition: time from speech instruction input to start of speech response, measured on 1 L40

metrics.name: Speech rate (WPS)
metrics.definition: average words per second of generated speech

metrics.name: Human evaluation
metrics.definition: side-by-side win/tie/lose on helpfulness and naturalness; 20 instructions, 5 participants, 100 votes per comparison

eval.protocol: InstructS2S-Eval, 199 instructions, greedy single run, GPT-4o judge; offline and streaming scenarios; no seeds or significance tests; human eval on 20 sampled instructions vs the two cascades

prompts.text:
<|begin of text|><|start header id|>system<|end header id|>
You are a helpful language and speech assistant. You are able to understand the speech content that the user provides, and assist the user with a variety of tasks using natural language. <|eot id|>
<|start header id|>user<|end header id|>
<speech>
Please answer the questions in the user’s input speech. <|eot id|>
<|start header id|>assistant<|end header id|>

Below is an instruction data containing the user’s instruction. I would like to generate a speech version of this instruction for training a large language model that supports speech input. Therefore, please rewrite my instruction data according to the following requirements:
1. Modify the instruction to simulate human speech, adding fillers as appropriate (but not too many ‘you know’, ‘like’, etc.).
2. The question should not contain content that cannot be synthesized by the TTS model. Numbers should be written in English words rather than Arabic numerals.
3. The question should be relatively brief without excessive verbiage.
[instruction]: {instruction}
Please output in JSON format as follows: {“question”: {question}}.

Below is the transcribed text of a user’s speech query. Please provide a response to this question, which will be converted to speech using TTS. Please follow these requirements for your response:
1. Your response should not contain content that cannot be synthesized by the TTS model, such as parentheses, ordered lists, etc. Numbers should be written in English words rather than Arabic numerals.
2. Your response should be very concise and to the point, avoiding lengthy explanations.
[instruction]: {instruction}
Please output in JSON format as follows: {“response”: {response}}.

evidence.quote: we train the speech adapter and the LLM with a batch size of 32 for 3 epochs

results.claim: Minimum response latency of 236ms (Omega=10), below GPT-4o's quoted 320ms average audio latency.
results.setup: Streaming scenario, Omega=10, 1 NVIDIA L40 GPU, greedy search, InstructS2S-Eval (199 instructions)
results.quote: LLaMA-Omni can achieve a minimum latency of 236ms (with Ω= 10), which is even lower than GPT-4o’s average audio latency of 320ms.
results.note: Table 4 gives 236.18 ms total = 206.03 LLM + 30.15 vocoder. Abstract says 236ms. GPT-4o 320ms is not measured here.

results.claim: LLaMA-Omni scores highest on speech-to-text instruction following (ChatGPT Score) offline.
LLaMA-Omni scores highest on speech-to-speech instruction following (ChatGPT Score) offline.
results.setup: InstructS2S-Eval offline, speech transcribed with Whisper-large-v3 then GPT-4o scored
results.note: Margin over cascades is small (3.47 vs 3.40 vs 3.38); drop from S2TIF is 0.52 vs 0.04 and 0.09 for cascades.

results.claim: Speech-text alignment (ASR-WER) of LLaMA-Omni is worse than cascades but far better than SpeechGPT.
results.note: Unit of WER not stated explicitly (percent assumed).

results.claim: LLaMA-Omni has highest UTMOS offline (speech naturalness).
Training takes about 65 hours on 4 NVIDIA L40 GPUs.
results.quote: The entire training process takes approximately 65 hours on 4 NVIDIA L40 GPUs.
results.note: Abstract says less than 3 days on just 4 GPUs.

results.claim: At Omega=100 the latency is 563ms and metrics are close to offline.
results.quote: At a latency of 563ms (Ω= 100), the results of all metrics are relatively close to those in the offline scenario.

results.claim: SpeechGPT streaming latency exceeds 4500ms because it generates text instruction and response before units.
results.quote: its decoding latency is significantly higher than other systems (>4500ms)
results.note: Table 5: 4929.65 ms at Omega=10; offline 18090.45 ms.

results.claim: Smaller Omega lowers UTMOS (3.2304 at Omega=10 vs 3.8242 at Omega=100) because of more discontinuities; ChatGPT Score and ASR-WER change only slightly.

Human evaluation (20 instructions, 5 participants, 100 votes per comparison) favours LLaMA-Omni (Omega=40, 347ms) over SALMONN+Orca (Theta=3, 352ms) and Qwen2-Audio+Orca (Theta=3, 420ms) on helpfulness and naturalness.
results.note: Figure 4 bar labels (50/20/30, 48/28/24 helpfulness; 42/20/38, 44/33/23 naturalness) were not mapped to systems reliably from text extraction, so no value is recorded. Text refers to 'Figure 5' but the figure is Figure 4.

results.claim: Dataset InstructS2S-200K totals 418h of instructions and 1058h of responses.

limits: Only 199 instructions in the eval set, single greedy run, GPT-4o judge; no significance tests.
S2SIF is judged through Whisper ASR transcripts, so ASR errors lower scores.
Speech decoder is trained on only about 1K hours; authors concede ASR-WER higher than cascades with industrial TTS.
Responses use one standard voice (VITS/LJSpeech); expressiveness of speech not addressed (future work).
Latency excludes full-duplex or real-time interruption; authors plan to improve real-time interaction.
The 320ms GPT-4o latency is a quoted figure, not measured under the same conditions.
Human eval is small (20 instructions, 5 raters).
